canonical_data: in-process conversation/session state (step history, tool calls) held by the host application; no durable store is documented
current_repo_note: The repository's own README states cloning it is not sufficient to run the SDK: the package depends on a compiled runtime binary bundled only in the platform-specific wheels published to PyPI. The reviewed Apache-2.0 LICENSE text covers the Python wrapper source in this repository; neither the repository nor the PyPI project page states separate terms for that binary, so source_model is recorded as unclear rather than mixed_source (no proprietary terms were found to cite) or open_source (the binary that actually runs the agent loop ships no source).
strengths: Declarative hook/policy system (deny/allow/ask_user per tool) with a documented read-only default gives developers control before enabling write capabilities
Custom Python-function tools, MCP server integration, and scheduled triggers are first-class, documented primitives rather than bolt-ons
A layered architecture (Agent, Conversation/Session, Connection/Adapter) exposes both a batteries-included entry point and low-level streaming step access
weaknesses: The agent loop itself executes inside a compiled binary that ships only through the PyPI wheel and is absent from the source repository; neither the repository nor the PyPI project page documents separate terms for it, leaving its license status undocumented
No durable session store, crash recovery, or persistence layer is documented; state lives in the host process's memory for the life of the Conversation object
Tightly coupled to Google Gemini/Vertex AI (Express or Standard mode); no alternative model backend is documented
why_it_matters: The embeddable, code-first counterpart to Google's Antigravity desktop platform: developers who want the same agent loop inside their own application, rather than Antigravity's IDE/desktop surface, get a Python SDK instead of a GUI product.
